_about: 787-10, from Boeing D6-58333 Rev Q 2.2.3 (page index 22): side, plan and front views on one sheet, a picture (about 46 px a meter at scale 8). Line centres. The 787-9's points moved by the two plugs onto this sheet and snapped (b78x/*.anchors.json). Scaled by the printed 68.30 m overall length from the nose to the tail cone's tip; the drawn doors 1, 2 and 4 then land within 0.1 m of the door-location table (2.7.1). Door 3 (hidden behind the wing in the drawing) and the forward and aft cargo doors (drawn only as dotted sides) are placed from the table, at the 787-9's sizes; the windows behind the wing's lines at the drawing's pitch. The cockpit panes are the 787-9's (the same nose; this sheet draws them too coarsely to read).

sources.title: Boeing, 787 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58333 Rev Q, October 2025), 2.2.3 General Dimensions: Model 787-10; 2.7.1 Door Locations
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the side, plan and front views (tools/trace/b78x/), starting from the 787-9's points moved by the two fuselage plugs; the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. Door 3 and the forward and aft cargo doors are placed from the door-location table; the cockpit panes are the 787-9's (the same nose). The sheet prints the engine 9.71 m out; its own drawing has it at 9.92 m, where the 787-9's sheet prints 9.91 m for the same wing, so the shape keeps the drawing's.
